articles.title: JD Vance told Republicans to stop criticizing Ramaswamy's ad. Some aren't listening.
articles.summary: Vice President Vance defended GOP gubernatorial nominee Vivek Ramaswamy amid bipartisan criticism of an ad that features the estranged mother of his Democratic opponent. - Clipped From Video Some leading Ohio Republicans began distancing themselves from a controversial new ad from their gubernatorial nominee, Vivek Ramaswamy, even as the president and vice president defended it. Vice President JD Vance warned Republicans on Wednesday not to break ranks over the commercial, telling them to “stop whining” about it. And President Donald Trump, who endorsed Ramaswamy early in the Ohio primary, told reporters at the White House he “didn’t know anything about it” but heard “the mother went very rogue on the daughter.” “It’s a very unusual situation,” Trump said. The viral ad has drawn bipartisan criticism for featuring the estranged mother of his Democratic opponent, Amy Acton. In it, Acton’s mother called her daughter a liar and urged voters not to support her. Acton has said she has not seen her mother since she was about 12 years old, when she says the man her mother married sexually abused her. He faced criminal charges and was “declared a fugitive,” Acton said. “I would not have run that ad,” Sen. Jon Husted, a key Ohio Republican who is in one of the country’s most competitive Senate races, said in a statement to the Associated Press published shortly after appearing at a Cincinnati rally with Vance and Ramaswamy. Another top Ohio Republican, Secretary of State Frank LaRose, told the ABC affiliate in Columbus that he “probably wouldn’t run an ad like that.” LaRose is running for state auditor. At least one other GOP candidate in Ohio personally asked Ramaswamy not to air the controversial ad, a GOP operative told CNN. For months, Ramaswamy has largely run behind other candidates in the state in polling, and now there is a sense he could further jeopardize the GOP’s brand with a last-minute stunt to drum up base support, the source said. “Republicans in the state probably couldn’t be more pissed at him,” the operative told CNN. But another GOP operative downplayed the impact Ramaswamy could have, arguing that because he was running behind other candidates already, some of the concerns about him may already be baked in among GOP voters. What Vance said On Wednesday morning, Vance, a former Ohio senator, instructed his fellow Republicans to set aside any reservations about the ad. “Politics is a tough business, and my message to my fellow elected Republicans is if you actually believe in the things you say you believe in, stop whining about an advertisement and go win the race in 13 days,” Vance said at a news conference in Cincinnati. unknown content item - The initial video – which was shared widely on social media, including by the president’s eldest son, Donald Trump Jr. – has been roiling the gubernatorial race since it first showed up on social media, bringing the abuse Acton said she suffered at the hands of her stepfather to the forefront. Until Wednesday afternoon, the GOP criticism of the ad was mainly coming from national figures like Nikki Haley, who ran against Ramaswamy for president in 2024. But the comments by Husted and LaRose began to show cracks in the relative quiet among Ohio Republicans. Asked about the ad at the news conference, Vance declined to weigh in on its appropriateness but said he was “a little bit disgusted” that some Republicans appeared more outraged about it than they are about Democrats and their policies. Speaking later at a rally in Cincinnati that Ramaswamy attended, Vance brought up the ad on his own. He argued it was a justified response because Democrats have used “every dirty trick in the political book” against Ramaswamy. “Now the media and the Democrats in the state of Ohio are obsessed because guess what? Vivek Ramaswamy had the audacity to run a TV commercial which calls it out like it is and calls Amy Acton a liar,” Vance said. Ryan Smith, the former GOP speaker of the Ohio House of Representatives, pushed back against Vance’s criticism of fellow Republicans responding to the ad. “Stop normalizing bad behavior and embarrassing the party,” Smith wrote on X . “Ohio deserves better than this!” Ramaswamy’s campaign leaned into the controversy over the ad Tuesday night, announcing it would spend $4 million to run the spot. “She’s lied her entire life,” Donna Arthur says in the minute-long spot. “My daughter needs help, and she can’t help you if she needs help herself. People can change, but first they have to tell the truth, and my daughter still isn’t doing that.” The video was first published widely on Monday night by an Ohio political blogger, D.J. Byrnes, who is known as “The Rooster.” Byrnes told CNN he obtained the video from a voter who saw it as part of a poll and recorded it. On Tuesday morning, Acton’s campaign released a statement from her brother, Philip Stearns, denouncing the video and linking it to Ramaswamy. “It’s not surprising that Vivek Ramaswamy has stooped to such a despicable low as to attempt to turn the sexual abuse Amy endured at twelve years old from our birth mother’s husband into a political talking point,” Stearns said. “After he was arrested and Amy and I were removed from their custody, our birth mother stayed married to Amy’s rapist until he died.” Later Tuesday, Acton’s campaign released a new ad featuring Stearns making similar points. “Shame on Vivek,” he says in the spot. unknown content item - Ad did not initially have political disclaimer Ramaswamy’s campaign initially did not confirm their involvement in the ad Tuesday, saying only that Ohioans “deserve to know” what Acton’s mother says about her daughter. But later in the day, Ramaswamy confirmed, “It is an ad from our campaign.” The incendiary spot will run on TV and streaming platforms, according to a spokesperson for the Ramaswamy campaign, Connie Luck. Axios first reported that news. from social media When it first circulated, the video did not have the standard disclaimer that political ads carry saying who paid for or authorized them, nor did it show up Tuesday morning as a paid ad in the race on AdImpact, the political ad-tracking service. And the first Ramaswamy campaign statement from Luck did not address whether it was responsible for the video. It suggested voters should consider the message from Acton’s mother and repeated her attack, asserting that “we know that Amy Acton is a serial fabulist who has some serious problems with the truth that the public needs to be aware of before deciding who to entrust as governor.” The statement went on to argue that people who know Acton well — including “her own mother” — “are clearly warning Ohioans not to vote for her.” “Ohioans deserve to know that,” Luck said. An official with V-PAC, the main super PAC backing Ramaswamy, said it did not make the video. CNN has attempted to contact Arthur for more information about how the video came together. Ramaswamy was heckled at a campaign event Tuesday evening by a person appearing to cite the viral video. Within seconds of Ramaswamy taking the stage at a Columbus-area town hall, an audience member rose up and began yelling at him, making a reference to “Amy Acton’s mother” and the abuse that the candidate says she suffered from her mother’s husband at a young age. “Sir, if you want to be patient and you want to ask a question at the end, you’re free to do that,” Ramaswamy said as the man was escorted out. “Thank you for your contribution today.” Speaking with reporters after the event, Ramaswamy took responsibility for the ad and reiterated that voters should take into account what people who know Acton “well” are saying about her. He said he has never met the mother and that she was “not compensated” for the ad. unknown content item - Acton herself weighed in during an interview with WOSU Public Media . “It’s awful to see her this way, and it’s even more incredible to see that my opponent (Ramaswamy) has taken advantage of someone who’s clearly not well, who is older, and this is totally in line with who he is,” Acton said. Her criticism joined the growing chorus. Haley, Ramaswamy’s 2024 primary rival, said the ad was the latest evidence that Ramaswamy is “a bad guy.” “It’s a shame he continues to get away with it,” she wrote on X . Meghan McCain, the daughter of the late Arizona GOP Sen. John McCain, said on X that the ad was “dastardly” and “never should have been created.” Sherrod Brown, the Democratic nominee for Senate in Ohio, said on X that the video was “disgusting” and that Husted should condemn it. The Democratic Governors Association said in a statement that the video was part of a “relentless smear campaign” that Ramaswamy has waged against Acton. Acton and Ramaswamy are locked in one of the most competitive governor’s races in the country, vying to replace term-limited Republican Mike DeWine. The ads in the race have been especially nasty, fueling a controversial decision by Acton to decline to debate Ramaswamy. Republican candidates in the state are preparing for a statewide bus tour starting Friday. DeWine’s office also has not commented on the ad. He defended Acton earlier in the campaign against criticism about Acton’s work as state public health director during the Covid-19 pandemic. A member of DeWine’s Cabinet, Lydia Mihalik, said Tuesday on X that the ad crossed a line. “We can disagree on plenty of things without losing our sense of decency,” said Mihalik, director of the state’s Department of Development. “I don’t have to agree with Amy Acton’s politics to believe that exploiting someone’s childhood trauma is wrong.” Nick Owens, a Republican activist in Ohio, told CNN the ad is “frankly despicable” and would help Acton raise “a lot of money.” Owens, who calls himself a lifelong Republican, is a former county GOP chair in the state who’s been organizing opposition to data centers. Acton, the former Ohio public health director, has spoken before about her estrangement from her mother and hardscrabble childhood. In a 2019 interview with the Youngstown Vindicator , she said her mother married a man when she was between ages 9 and 12 who abused her and who faced criminal charges. The family was living in a tent at a campground outside Youngstown at the time. According to legal documents provided by the Acton campaign, Acton’s allegations against her stepfather emerged in July of 1978 when her father testified to police his daughter was sexually abused by her stepfather. A day later, her stepfather was arrested for rape. He pleaded not guilty but was indicted by a grand jury in September of that year. By October, prosecutors asked for a warrant for his arrest. In the early 1980s, one record shows authorities were still looking for him, but there is no record of any further action in the case. “I was lucky that it got bad enough, because it got me out of there,” Acton told the Vindicator. She said the last time she saw her mother was at the courthouse when she tried to give her a kiss and Acton rejected her. This story has been updated with additional information. CNN’s Lauren Fox and Kit Maher contributed to this report. articles.title: Canadian airlines are cutting flight routes amid weakening demand for U.S. travel
articles.summary: Weakening demand for U.S. travel is prompting Canadian airlines to cut flights south of the border, with Air Canada canceling five routes for 2027. Data from aviation data and analytics company Cirium shows that the airline, Canada ’s flag carrier and the largest in the country by fleet size and passenger volume, has cut its flights from Montréal to Seattle, Toronto to Boston and Charleston, and Vancouver to Nashville and Raleigh-Durham. The service between Toronto and Charleston, which the company started in March 2024, was the only Air Canada flight bringing Canadian snowbirds to South Carolina , one of the most popular U.S. states for their neighbors’ winter escapes. An Air Canada Rouge Boeing 737 MAX 8 approaches Los Angeles International Airport during a flight from Vancouver on September 18, 2026. These are the routes to U.S. destinations canceled by Air Canada next year: Montréal-Trudeau International Airport (YUL) to Seattle–Tacoma International Airport (SEA); Billy Bishop Toronto City Centre Airport (YTZ) to Boston Logan International Airport (BOS); Vancouver International Airport (YVR) to Nashville International Airport (BNA); Vancouver International Airport (YVR) to Raleigh–Durham International Airport (RDU); Toronto Pearson International Airport (YYZ) to Charleston International Airport (CHS). According to aviation website SimpleFlying, three of the routes were already suspended—from Montréal to Seattle, Vancouver to Nashville, and Vancouver to Raleigh-Durham—but were supposed to be reinstated in May 2027. However, all flights have now been removed. Flights from Toronto to Charleston, also already suspended, were supposed to start again in April next year, but they have been removed as well. According to SimpleFlying, only 66.5 percent of seats on flights between the two destinations were filled between March 2024 and July 2026, falling from 67.8 percent in the first year of service to 62.1 percent in 2025, despite fewer flights and less capacity. An Air Canada representative confirmed the suspension of the seasonal flight to Charleston to TheStreet. On the other hand, Air Canada announced it will resume flights from Toronto to Kentucky’s Louisville Muhammad Ali International Airport (SDF), which were last available in 2002. Newsweek contacted Air Canada for comment by email on Thursday morning. Other Canadian Airlines Have Already Withdrawn from the US Market As Canadian travel to the U.S. remains under pressure from the simmering political tension between the Trump administration and the Canadian government and from rising fuel prices, other companies have already drastically reduced services to the United States. Westjet, Canada’s second-largest airline, has cut 10 U.S. routes this year, according to Cirium data cited by SimpleFlying. Flights from Edmonton International Airport were the most affected, with services to Atlanta, Nashville, Chicago, Seattle and San Francisco halted this year. Flights between Edmonton and Nashville and Chicago were only operative for one season. A WestJet airplane takes off from Calgary, Canada, on January 21, 2021. The company also cut three routes between Vancouver International Airport and Boston, Nashville and Lihue, Hawaii, leaving the Canadian city without direct service to the latter. WestJet also cut its nonstop service between Toronto Pearson and Los Angeles in April, and removed the service from Winnipeg to Nashville in May. Montréal-headquartered airline Air Transat ended all its flights to the U.S. by mid-June, which had been reduced by then to two destinations: Florida’s Fort Lauderdale and Orlando. Flights from Montréal to Orlando ended on May 3, while flights from Quebec City and Montréal to Fort Lauderdale ended between May and June. Newsweek contacted WestJet and Air Transat for comment by email on Thursday morning. Why Are Canadian Airlines Cancelling Routes? The number of Canadians traveling to the U.S. has plummeted since President Donald Trump’s return to the White House. Even though travel rebounded slightly last year, new figures show that the decline has not stopped. According to the latest data by the Canadian government’s statistics agency, the number of Canadian cross-border trips last month was down by 29 percent compared with two years ago in 2024, with car border crossings down by 31 percent and air travel down by 19 percent. The pullback by Canadian travelers appears to reflect a combination of political backlash and weaker purchasing power, while decisions by airlines to cut back on services would appear to be straightforward common sense for carriers that want to stay afloat while facing dwindling demand. Trump’s calls for Canada to become the “51st state” have angered many Canadians who had already turned sour on his administration after the imposition of sweeping tariffs on Canadian goods, pushing many to avoid traveling south of the border. President Donald Trump is pictured with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney during a work lunch at the G7 summit in Evian, France, on June 16, 2026. It is also a decision that makes financial sense to many travelers, as a weak Canadian dollar has been making U.S. holidays more expensive. The Canadian dollar has weakened throughout 2026: it began the year at about $0.729 and had fallen to around $0.71 by Thursday. With fewer travelers choosing American destinations, airlines have responded by cutting capacity. Aviation intelligence provider OAG reported that Canadian carriers cut U.S.-bound capacity by nearly 10 percent in the first quarter of 2026, equivalent to about 450,000 seats, as demand moved away from traditional American sun destinations. Instead, Canadian airlines are shifting services to European and Caribbean destinations, which have seen a rise in demand. In the first quarter of the year, according to OAG, capacity from Canada to Costa Rica rose 15 percent and to Mexico by 5 percent, an increase which likely reflects “a shift in leisure travel demand from traditional U.S. sun destinations,” the company wrote. articles.title: Super Typhoon Champi intensifies into one of the year's most powerful storms
articles.summary: Authorities in Taiwan issued a land warning Thursday as Typhoon Champi closed in, and is expected to hit the northeast of the island. Taiwan's transport ministry said 125 flights, mostly domestic, were canceled Thursday. In Japan, Japan Airlines, ANA and Skymark have canceled more than 100 flights through Sunday, disrupting travel for more than 11,000 passengers, Reuters reported. However, the interior ministry said no evacuations had been reported. Super Typhoon Champi was recorded as one of the strongest storms on Earth in 2026 on Wednesday, but weakened slightly on Thursday. The tropical cyclone tied April's Super Typhoon Sinlaku for the strongest 1-minute sustained winds of 2026, at 185 mph, which is equivalent to a Category 5 hurricane. The typhoon is still packing gusts of more than 227 kph (141 mph) near its center, according to Taiwan's Central Weather Administration (CWA). The Joint Typhoon Warning Center classifies a storm as a super typhoon when its 1-minute sustained winds reach at least 150 mph. That threshold falls within the Category 4 hurricane range. "A tropical cyclone is a generic term used by meteorologists to describe a rotating, organized system of clouds and thunderstorms that originates over tropical or subtropical waters and has closed, low-level circulation," according to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration . The main difference between hurricanes and typhoons is geographic: Storms in the Northwest Pacific are called typhoons, while those in the North Atlantic and central and eastern North Pacific are called hurricanes. What is Champi's path? As of 11 a.m. Thursday, Champi was about 520 km (320 miles) southeast of Taiwan's southern tip. It is forecast to pass the northeast, then curve north toward China's coast and later into southern Japan, with its closest approach to Taiwan expected Friday. Its radius has widened to 320 km (199 miles), enough to reach most of the island. Forecasters said the effects could last nearly two days, with heavy rain likely to continue in the north and center after the storm moves away Saturday afternoon. The storm, which is barreling across the western Pacific Ocean, is expected to brush past the island's northeastern coast and gradually weaken as it approaches, passing northeastern Taiwan, turning north toward the Chinese coast and eventually moving into southern Japan, Reuters reported. The storm is forecast to make a slight turn toward the northwest and weaken through Thursday. Super Typhoon Champi's path. Naval Meteorology and Oceanography Command What are the expected impacts? Champi is expected to bring heavy rain and strong winds to parts of Taiwan and eastern China through the weekend, according to AccuWeather senior meteorologist Jason Nicholls. Heavy rain is expected to affect Taiwan from Thursday night (Oct. 22) into Saturday (Oct. 24) and east-central China from Friday night (Oct. 23) through Sunday (Oct. 25). Rainfall is forecast to total up to 18 inches, with the heaviest rain expected in northeastern Taiwan. Experts expect the typhoon to impact the island for two days, and have issued mobile phone alerts warning of waves of more than 6 meters (20 feet) in coastal towns, while total rainfall of nearly one meter (3 feet) was expected in northern mountain areas, including the hills near the capital Taipei, Reuters reported. The heavy rain could cause flooding, mudslides, structural damage and transportation delays, according to AccuWeather. Strong winds from Champi, with wind gusts up to 120 mph, are expected to affect Taiwan and eastern China from Thursday night into Sunday. The winds could cause structural damage, prolonged power outages and transportation delays. articles.title: U.S. reportedly considering major strikes on Iran after the midterms
articles.summary: The national flag of Iran hangs on a building damaged by the U.S.-Israeli attacks in Tehran, Iran, on April 20, 2026. —Shadati—Xinhua/Getty Images The U.S. and Israel are reportedly developing plans for major strikes on Iran after the U.S. midterm elections in November. Citing people familiar with the deliberations, the New York Times reported on Wednesday that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth discussed the possibility of renewed strikes on Iran with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in Israel this week. Possible targets of the strikes reportedly include Iran’s energy infrastructure, nuclear facilities, and missile and drone arsenal. TIME has reached out to the White House for comment. U.S. officials have repeatedly asserted that the Iranian Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps are teetering on the edge of collapse but are deliberately prolonging the war in an effort to meddle with Republican prospects in the midterm elections. Once the elections are over, President Donald Trump promised last month, the Iranian regime would quickly capitulate. “I think the war is going to end immediately after the election,” Trump said. “They can’t hold out any longer.” Renewed strikes could complicate that outlook. Some officials have reportedly argued that resuming attacks for an intense but limited campaign would hasten Iran’s economic collapse, especially as the country has been squeezed by an ongoing U.S. blockade on Iranian ports and economic sanctions campaign . The officials hope the blow will make Iran more amenable to negotiations. Trump has at times shared that view. Last week, Trump told Newsmax he was considering additional military action in Iran, including a possible strike on Iran’s Pickaxe Mountain , a nuclear facility deep underground. His comments came amid reports that he was weighing deploying a 22,000 GBU-43/B Massive Ordnance Air Blast bomb, also known as the “mother of all bombs.” The President added the war would end soon, be it through negotiation or escalation. “Do I annihilate the Islamic Republic and do it quickly, never giving them a chance to kill and destroy people and countries again? Do I drive them into hell with no chance of survival and no hope of future greatness or generations?” he said in a speech to the United Nations General Assembly last month. “But I believe we’ll make a deal,” he added, “right after the election.” Will the U.S. renew strikes on Iran? Intensified fighting between the Iran-aligned Houthi rebels and the Saudi and Yemeni governments has threatened to create a broader regional crisis that could be harder to disengage from. The State Department on Wednesday ordered nonemergency government employees and their families to leave Saudi Arabia amid escalating attacks by the Houthis on Saudi infrastructure. Houthi attacks on Saudi airports and Aramco facilities, as well as their attempts to disrupt shipping through Bab El-Mandeb , which has become an important alternative to the Strait of Hormuz for energy trade , could prompt direct U.S. strikes in support of Saudi Arabia, analysts have said. Trump said earlier this month that the U.S. “may” join Saudi strikes on the Houthis, although that has yet to transpire. Israel’s Oct. 27 election could also raise the stakes of additional military action. Netanyahu , whom Trump has endorsed , would remain in office until a new government is formed, even if his bloc loses the election, and his government would retain the authority to order strikes during that transition. But renewed strikes before the election, or after an electoral defeat, could invite scrutiny. “One ordered in the last weeks of a deadlocked campaign would be judged in Israel as politics as well as strategy,” Gregg Roman, executive director of the Middle East Forum, wrote in a September analysis. Nevertheless, the forum assessed that a large-scale Israeli strike on Iranian territory, with or without U.S. participation, was probable before the end of the year. Analysts told the Times Netanyahu could use the prospect of joint strikes to form a unity government that could allow him to stay in power. “The larger constraint,” Roman argued, “is Washington.” Trump has not yet approved the proposed strikes, the Times reported. Trump has also called off plans to renew attacks on Iran before. He reportedly blocked an Israeli plan for a multi-day offensive against Iran earlier this month, and rejected five proposals for major operations against Iran or the Houthis in recent months. The U.S. and Iran have not exchanged major fighting in recent weeks. The last reported U.S. strikes on Iran were on Sept. 8, even as Iranian attacks on commercial shipping have continued. Earlier this month, Trump ruled out attacking Iran before the midterms. Read More: What Is the Status of the U.S.-Iran Peace Talks? Here's What Both Sides Are Saying How might Iran respond to new strikes? Tehran’s reluctance to make concessions to the U.S. appears to have strengthened, rather than weakened, over the course of the war. Iranian leaders reiterated this week that they will not directly negotiate with the U.S. unless Washington accedes to certain demands , which include ending its naval blockade and releasing frozen Iranian funds. The initial U.S. and Israeli bombing campaign on Iran that began the war on Feb. 28, as well as June 2025 attacks during an earlier round of U.S.-Iran nuclear diplomacy, also hardened the Iranian view that the U.S. is not serious about negotiating. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said in March that the previous disruptions of negotiating rounds had increased distrust in Washington . Last month, the IRGC published an open letter appealing to American voters to “wrest control” from their government. In the letter, the IRGC said: “Despite all the hardships that our enemies impose on us, we will continue fighting, as we have done for the past 47 years.” Both the U.S. and Iran appear to believe they hold enough leverage to achieve their goals, and those “dueling perceptions” have impeded progress towards a deal, according to an Oct. 1 analysis by the New York-based nonpartisan research organization The Soufan Center. Iran’s key point of leverage is its blockade of the Strait of Hormuz , a narrow waterway vital to global energy trade. Iran’s militarization of the strait has disrupted global oil and liquefied natural gas supplies, leading to soaring energy prices and inflation. Analysts previously told TIME that the higher prices are politically costly for Trump. In recent weeks, a growing number of Republicans have broken with Trump on Iran. The President has also seen his lowest approval ratings of his second term. Iran’s ability to choke off regional oil exports, however, appears to be waning. Middle East oil exports topped prewar levels last week as shipping companies use alternative routes to bypass the Strait of Hormuz. HSBC Group Chief Executive Georges Elhedery also projected that Hormuz could be “redundant” in five years thanks to investment in alternative logistics routes. Iranian officials told the Times that they are aware of the U.S. and Israel’s war planning and are developing their own tactics. Earlier this week, IRGC spokesperson Hossein Mohebbi told the Tehran Times that “even a limited” attack from Washington would provoke a “serious energy crisis” for the world. Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei said that an attack on Pickaxe Mountain would be met with a response “just as hard,” if not “stronger.” And earlier this month, Iranian officials said Iran had prepared potential retaliatory operations that would depart from the U.S. and Israel’s assumptions. Security Chief Mohsen Rezaei told Press TV that Iran could respond to renewed attacks by targeting new targets, including U.S.-linked data centers and AI facilities in the Gulf, as well as subsea communications cables. Last month, Iran threatened to retaliate against any further U.S. attacks by targeting U.S. oil and gas assets in the Gulf. Read More: ‘One of the World’s Most Critical Digital Bottlenecks’: How the Iran War Could Threaten Global Internet Access In a post on Telegram on Sunday, Mahdi Mohammadi, a senior adviser to Iran’s negotiator Gen. Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, said, if the U.S. and Israel attack, “they may want to keep it short, but we will not allow it.” He added on Wednesday: “The war will continue longer and across a wider geography than the enemy calculates.” This article originally appeared on Time at https://time.com/article/2026/10/22/us-israel-iran-war-strikes-midterms/

articles.title: Elon Musk compared Tesla's robot to a toddler. Meta had a different AI surprise.
articles.summary: Earnings season is in full swing, and Big Tech calls are about more than the heavy use of "superintelligence," which some read as a bid to please the White House after it reportedly disliked the term "artificial intelligence." Here are three moments from the earnings calls of Tesla ( TSLA ), Meta ( META ), and IBM ( IBM ) on late Wednesday that stuck with us. Tesla Much of the focus today is on Tesla cutting its capital spending plans for this year to $20 billion from the $25 billion it guided to three months ago. A key factor appears to be that its Optimus robots need more training before they're released into the real world. Elon Musk said investors should think of Optimus as a baby: "A big difference with Optimus versus the cars is we don't have this vast fleet of cars from which we can gather training data. With Optimus, we have to bootstrap it by making the robots and having them do self-play, which is really how a human learns to navigate the world. You can see this when you have a toddler, and they grow up, and initially, they're sort of wobbly, and they don't know how to do things. Eventually they learn to wipe their own ass, which is a big milestone. As anyone who's had kids knows. Then they learn to read and do all sorts of things and be able to do these things. They learn this by playing. We actually need Optimus to play at scale in order to have it be really good at tasks in the real world." Meta Are early users of Meta's ( META ) Muse AI agent overspending? Mark Zuckerberg's comments on credit limits during the earnings call suggest they might be. That raises a bigger question: Could AI agent shopping end badly for retailers and banks, in the form of unpaid debts and write-offs? "The most common use case for Muse is shopping, with more than a quarter of people who are using Muse engaging in this with an average purchase size of over $200," Zuckerberg said on the call. "Plaid told us that they hadn't seen activity like they're seeing with their connector on any other service before. In the first week, we had to work with Stripe to raise credit limits since the volumes were above what any of us expected." IBM IBM ( IBM ) CEO Arvind Krishna seemed to be in a better place this earnings call compared to three months ago , which came on the heels of a shock earnings warning that sent the stock reeling. It was interesting to hear Krishna call out some C-suite concerns about the current spending on AI tools: "I think what we are seeing is that at least larger enterprises are becoming a lot more cognizant and a lot more aware of what is the true ROI of all of their AI spend. They are also getting worried if some of the AI spending completely out of control with no real return. But the way I have always characterized it is, there is no question to us, and this is the advice I give every C-suite member that I meet, that what we are trying to give people on AI, the productivity, the advantages of AI, the way it is going to change work, is very real. Let me not make any confusion around that." Brian Sozzi is Yahoo Finance's Executive Editor, host of the Sozzi Unleashed morning show and the Power Players with Brian Sozzi podcast, and a member of Yahoo Finance's editorial leadership team. articles.title: Pentagon quietly builds new agency to sabotage foreign military technology
articles.summary: The Pentagon has spent months quietly building an elite new tech agency to help covertly disrupt and sabotage foreign technology programs considered threats to American military superiority. Neither Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth nor any other senior Pentagon official has publicly mentioned the agency since it was established this April — a conspicuous omission for a department that has reveled in announcing other major changes aimed at modernizing the military or adopting hard-nosed new policies against foreign adversaries. Information on the Technology Support Office, or TSO as it is called internally, is nearly impossible to find on Pentagon websites, and the agency is mentioned by name only in several previously unreported Defense Department historical records and memoranda . While the specifics of its work are highly classified, POLITICO spoke with 12 current and former U.S. national security officials with varying degrees of knowledge about TSO to understand how the agency came to be, the broad contours of its mission and why its operations are shrouded in secrecy. Some of these people helped establish TSO or worked closely with it; others attended briefings or spoke with current Pentagon officials about it; and some were familiar with Defense Department intelligence programs now merged into TSO. All were granted anonymity to share sensitive details about the agency that have not been previously reported. Deputy Defense Secretary Steve Feinberg, a private equity billionaire and former head of the White House's Intelligence Advisory Board during President Donald Trump's first term, led the push inside the Pentagon to create the new agency. Tom Rakusan, a senior adviser to Feinberg at the Pentagon, has also been closely involved in setting up TSO. Rakusan is a longtime veteran of the CIA's clandestine service, and most recently worked at Feinberg's private equity firm, where he focused on emerging technology. Hegseth and Feinberg established TSO quickly and without attracting outside scrutiny because they largely built the agency by reorganizing two classified Pentagon intelligence programs that have conducted similar clandestine tech-sabotage efforts at a smaller scale since 2023. But by creating an agency dedicated to expanding that work, the Defense Department is signaling its intent to ramp up a range of aggressive covert activities abroad — potentially including cyberattacks, supply chain disruptions and disinformation operations. Many of the people who spoke to POLITICO argued that the aggressive new initiative is needed to help the Pentagon counter foreign adversaries they say are harnessing artificial intelligence and advanced commercial technologies, such as drones, in creative ways that could erode America's military advantage. "It is a refocus from the highest levels of the government on this type of activity, which has been sorely needed," said one former senior Pentagon intelligence official with direct knowledge of TSO. Others worry that the Trump administration has deliberately avoided public mention of TSO to avoid oversight over programs that could harm civilians or inflame tensions with adversary countries the U.S. is not at war with, such as China. To make an undertaking like TSO successful, said another former senior Pentagon official, "you have to pull off movie-level spy craft." "But the questions are: What are the approval structures, what is the oversight, who is read in to give the American people confidence that what you're doing is consistent with our values and you're not creating something that five years from now will be seen as incredibly problematic?" the official added. In response to a series of questions about TSO and the details of this story, Deputy Pentagon Press Secretary Jacob Bliss said, "This query appears to be built on information that is simply not true. Whoever is feeding you these claims are either badly misinformed or deliberately leading you astray to peddle their fantasies." The White House did not respond to a request for comment on this story. A move to 'centralize' control While TSO lacks the legal authority to conduct clandestine operations directly, it works closely with senior U.S. military and intelligence officers to develop cutting-edge tools and strategies to disrupt adversaries' access to critical defense technologies — or subvert them from afar. TSO is staffed with engineers, special operators and intelligence officers, and its work spans everything from building bespoke hacking tools to planning elaborate deception operations that trick adversaries into installing faulty components — likely designed by TSO — in key foreign weapons platforms. TSO's overarching goal is to "buy time or stop adversaries from developing technologies" that would most threaten the U.S. military in a major conflict, said a former U.S. intelligence official who worked closely with the agency. Pentagon staff had been exploring whether to create a new agency like TSO for more than a year. According to three former intelligence officials, staff in the Office of the Undersecretary of Defense for Intelligence and Security, or I&S, which oversees Defense Department intelligence programs, began work in early 2025 on a white paper exploring how to scale up the Pentagon's two existing classified tech sabotage programs. The white paper, completed that fall, considered nesting both programs under the Pentagon's digital warfighting unit, U.S. Cyber Command, but ultimately recommended merging the efforts into a new agency with its own budget and procurement powers. The move would empower the agency to more quickly integrate cutting-edge tech from the private sector and think more strategically about which foreign defense technologies pose the biggest threats across U.S. military organizations. Senior Pentagon leadership also saw an opportunity to consolidate some control over Defense Department intelligence programs, a former Pentagon official familiar with the initiative said. TSO is "definitely part of this move to centralize some control upstairs," the official explained. A new Pentagon power center The race to stand up the agency kicked off in earnest this spring. Feinberg signed a memo establishing TSO and placing it under the "authority, direction, and control" of the Undersecretary of War for Intelligence & Security on April 14, according to a monthly leadership publication from the Defense Department's public record-keeping office. The Senate confirmed the current head of I&S, Bradley Hansell, in July 2025. This summer, the Pentagon tapped Grant Hundley, a former Marine Corps special operations officer, to serve as TSO's director. They also selected William Nelson, a career Army official recently at Army Futures Command, as the new Director of Intelligence for Sensitive Activities and Special Programs, who will work with Hansell to oversee the agency internally from I&S. It's unclear how much money has been allocated to carry out TSO's secretive operations, or if it has issued any new contracts yet. A second former Pentagon official and a former U.S. national security official said the agency has told some defense contractors it's interested in offensive hacking capabilities. The former senior Pentagon intelligence official estimated that its budget for classified contracts alone is likely north of $1.5 billion. They are seeking contractors on "the leading edge of technology," that official said, and hope to procure "a whole host of tools wherever your imagination can go." Bliss did not respond to a request for comment on whether the Pentagon has requested additional money to fund the agency or if it intends to seek long-term authorization from Congress. Beyond offensive operations, TSO will also focus on coordinating technology use and cutting red tape for defense contractors spread across a thicket of heavily siloed Pentagon intelligence programs. According to one former U.S. intelligence official who has spoken with Pentagon leadership, one such initiative would see TSO build a central "catalog" of approved commercial AI and tech tools contractors could use on classified initiatives. The agency's emergence as a power center for military hacking and sabotage has irked some senior officials elsewhere in the Pentagon. Special Operations Command and U.S. Cyber Command both objected to creating the new agency, fearing it would cut into their budgets, according to the two former intelligence officials and one former senior U.S. national security official. The two former intelligence officials added that friction over TSO is part of the reason why Cyber Command's chief acquisition officer, Khoi Nguyen, recently left the command . Nguyen, whose former role had him overseeing the digital warfighting unit's efforts to procure cutting-edge hacking tools, did not reply to a request for comment. TSO, said the former intelligence official who worked closely with the agency, is taking on the types of operations Cyber Command "would love to claim as its own." 'Opportunities to hide and misdirect' Several people who spoke to POLITICO support TSO's mission but worry that the secrecy surrounding its work could embolden current Pentagon leadership to carry out missions that flout international law or funnel coveted classified contracts to political allies. Over the last two years, Hegseth has boasted publicly about operations that test the boundaries of domestic and international law , while slow-rolling Congressional attempts to oversee deadly missions that have gone awry. The Pentagon recently briefed some congressional officials on its plans for TSO, but only a small number of staffers have been read in on the initiative, said one current U.S. national security official, which could make it harder for Congress to identify any potential impropriety in TSO's operations or contracting. "Because it's a classified space, there's even more opportunities to hide or misdirect," the official said. In a statement, Bliss, the Pentagon spokesperson, said the Defense Department "values its longstanding working relationship with Congress" and "will continue working closely and constructively with the relevant committees to provide appropriate information, answer legitimate questions, and ensure Congress can fulfill its constitutional oversight responsibilities." Hegseth and Feinberg have announced a flurry of new modernization initiatives — such as a new commission dubbed Project Meridian led by SpaceX CEO Elon Musk and Anduril founder Palmer Luckey — that skeptics say expose the Defense Department to a torrent of conflicts of interest. Democrats have focused their concern on Feinberg because the private equity and venture capital firms he led before joining the Defense Department both have sizable investments in defense tech companies that compete for Pentagon contracts. Bliss called concern about conflicts of interest "a baseless, completely recycled narrative that certain reporters continue to lazily push despite having zero facts to support it." DOD, he added, "maintains a rigorous, multi-layered ethics framework that includes financial disclosure reviews, divestitures where appropriate, and screening to prevent conflicts of interest. Every DOW official is in full compliance with all ethical laws and regulations. Any claims otherwise are false." Other people who spoke to POLITICO said they felt reassured by the current and former career officials chosen to work most closely with the agency, specifically Nelson and Rakusan. These are "seasoned career professionals who have withstood political pressures before," said the former intelligence official who has spoken with Pentagon leadership about the initiative. articles.title: Websites worldwide go dark after AI discovers major security flaws
articles.summary: Security firm Calif found the flaws in August using OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol model (ANDREJ IVANOV) Governments and companies around the world shut down websites as they raced Thursday to protect themselves from hacks after artificial intelligence uncovered critical flaws in a widely used programming language called PHP. PHP helps run about 70 percent of the world's websites -- from online stores and news outlets to government services -- according to Wiz Research, one of the cybersecurity firms that found the two flaws. Created in the early 1990s, PHP originally stood for "personal home page" but now means "hypertext preprocessor" and sits underneath popular web design platforms. "These findings rank among the most severe vulnerabilities discovered in PHP, and arguably in software history," a Wiz blog post said. Increasingly powerful AI models can spot weak points in back-end computer code that have gone unnoticed by humans for years. That has heightened cybersecurity fears, with the number of software vulnerabilities discovered worldwide in 2026 on track to roughly double last year's record total. PHP programmers released a fix Wednesday, and the US National Security Agency told organizations to patch their sites immediately or pull vulnerable systems offline -- a call echoed by authorities from Japan to the European Union. A platform affiliated with China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology urged the same, warning of "two critical remote code execution vulnerabilities with severe impact" in PHP. Only sites that run PHP on their own servers are exposed. Many large platforms are built on other programming languages or use operators that could install the fix quickly and were able to stay online. Rahat Masood, senior lecturer in cybersecurity at the University of New South Wales, Sydney, described the discovery as "quite devastating." It could allow "attackers to get into your servers without any authorisation, without any username or password," she told AFP. "Once they are in the servers, they can do anything they want" -- from stealing sensitive information to modifying website content -- she added, urging institutions to "take it seriously." - 'New phase' - Government agency sites in countries from Australia to Finland and the Netherlands were among those that went dark, while services from insurance firms, transport operators and media outlets were under emergency maintenance. Popular apps, including a Pokemon sleep tracker, were also temporarily taken offline while the fix was implemented, while the foundation that runs Wikipedia warned users they could see outages while it addressed the flaws. "If you run PHP, it is imperative that you update now," the PHP Foundation, which funds developers working on the language, said in a blog post. Volker Dusch, a security engineer at the foundation, told the Wall Street Journal it was the most serious problem PHP had faced in more than a decade, comparing it to Heartbleed, a 2014 flaw that set off a worldwide rush to patch. Security firm Calif found the flaws in August using OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol model, as part of an OpenAI-funded audit of PHP's code. OpenAI said the discovery "marks a new phase, where AI can find security bugs with internet-scale impact." Wiz, which is owned by Google, said it found them independently weeks later with help from AI models including Google's Gemini 4 Argon and GPT-5.6 Sol. The flaws had been reported privately to PHP's developers and kept confidential while a fix was prepared. - AI fuels urgency - Details leaked online Tuesday, a day before the planned release of the fix -- prompting the rush to take sites offline before hackers could exploit them. Steve Kerrison, senior lecturer in cybersecurity at the Singapore campus of James Cook University, told AFP that the fear of hackers using AI to quickly and easily exploit the PHP vulnerabilities had fuelled urgency to react. So far there has been little evidence of damaging attacks, although data breaches could lead to a wave of so-called "phishing" attacks, where hackers use personal details to steal passwords, down the line. Larger institutions, from government agencies to news outlets, should be able to fix their websites relatively fast, Kerrison said -- but others may be left vulnerable. "There are sites, systems and people out there who will have no idea about this and still won't for days, weeks and months," Kerrison warned. That may include user-run blogs that could be weaponised to spread computer viruses, spam people or distribute malicious content, he said. arp-kaf/fox This article originally appeared on AFP at https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/websites-dark-worldwide-ai-exposes-171251949.html

articles.title: Russia pounds Kyiv with missiles and drones, hours after agreeing to peace talks
articles.summary: KYIV, Ukraine (AP) — Russia bombarded Kyiv with ballistic missiles in an hourslong nighttime barrage, while the Russian military said Thursday that its air defenses intercepted over 800 drones fired by Ukraine at Moscow and other cities. At least four people were killed in Ukraine and dozens of others were wounded, officials said, in the large-scale attacks that began only hours after Russian President Vladimir Putin agreed “in principle” on Wednesday to resume three-way negotiations between Russia, Ukraine and the United States . Putin's consent came in talks in St. Petersburg with U.S. President Donald Trump’s envoy, Steve Witkoff, who had spoken of a “new momentum” toward peace after meeting Tuesday with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Norway. No date was set for the tripartite talks. Representatives of the three countries held rounds of “technical” talks in the United Arab Emirates and Switzerland in January and February, seeking to lay the groundwork for detailed negotiations. But they reported little progress beyond exchanges of prisoners of war. Russia and Ukraine remain far apart in their terms for stopping the fighting despite U.S. efforts . Zelenskyy says only a meeting of leaders can end the deadlock. As for the prospect of more “technical talks” between delegations: “We’ll see what happens this time.” Zelenskyy sees ‘no change’ in Moscow's attitude Russia’s aerial attacks hit 12 regions of Ukraine overnight, killing at least four people and wounding scores of others, including five children, Zelenskyy said on social media Thursday. Two women aged 50 and 60 were killed and dozens of others wounded in a Russian strike on a market in Lozova, in Ukraine’s northeastern Kharkiv region, said Oleh Syniehubov, head of the regional military administration. Another person was killed in other strikes on Kharkiv, the State Emergency Service said. The Ukrainian capital endured a noisy night as 21 ballistic missiles came in three waves, Zelenskyy said, smashing apartment buildings, energy facilities, a railway station and the Kyiv subway system, shopping malls and businesses. One person was killed in Kyiv. A Russian ballistic missile carrying cluster munitions — bombs that open in the air and release scores of smaller bomblets — targeted downtown Kyiv, said Serhii Beskrestnov, an adviser to Zelenskyy. Ukrainians are bracing for the bitterly cold months ahead as the recent escalation in Russian attacks targets the power grid to deny civilians heat, light and running water. Ukraine says Russia is stockpiling ballistic missiles for an annual campaign Ukrainians describe as “ weaponizing winter. ” The Russian bombardment showed “there has been no real change in (Moscow’s) attitude toward everything that is happening,” Zelenskyy said. Putin mulls attending G20 in Miami, Kremlin says The Ukrainian leader has pleaded with Washington to supply more Patriot air defense ammunition to stop the ballistic missiles, and to heap more sanctions on Russia to pressure Moscow to pursue peace. Instead, Trump has agreed with Putin to import diesel from Russia and waived heavy sanctions on Moscow, while U.S. officials say Patriot ammunition is in short supply. Western analysts say Putin wants to cut out Europe and Kyiv and negotiate Ukraine’s future directly with Washington. The Trump administration has also disparaged Europe. Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said Thursday that Putin had received an invitation to attend the G20 summit in Miami in December but hasn’t yet decided whether to go. “The American administration is doing a lot to help a peaceful settlement,” Peskov told reporters. “European capitals are doing nothing to promote a peaceful resolution, and they are doing a great deal to provoke the further escalation of fighting." Ukrainians chide Trump envoy for flattering Putin Witkoff, the Trump envoy who met with Putin in St. Petersburg on Wednesday, was harshly criticized in Ukraine and in the U.S. for praising the Russian leader as a “humanitarian” for ordering the release of a retired American teacher who was imprisoned on charges of fighting as a mercenary in Ukraine. Assassination attempts against Putin's foes — routinely denied by the Kremlin — have been common during his decades in power. And as the five-year anniversary of Russia’s all-out invasion of its neighbor approaches, aerial strikes have killed thousands of civilians and hundreds of thousands of soldiers. The latest “brutal” Russian attacks demonstrate “what Russian ‘humanism’ truly sounds like,” Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said on social media. “Appeasement, servility, and flattery will not stop this war. Only strength will.” Russia says it intercepted more than 800 Ukrainian drones Russia’s Defense Ministry said that air defenses overnight downed 808 Ukrainian drones, with two people reported wounded. Moscow’s Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said that 630 of the drones were fired toward the Russian capital between late Wednesday and early Thursday. Moscow airports temporarily restricted air traffic overnight. The Russian military hit the facilities involved in making and storing drones and cruise missiles and transport infrastructure in Kyiv in overnight strikes, the Defense Ministry said. Infrastructure in the southern port of Odesa and vessels used for the Ukrainian armed forces were also hit, it said. In other developments, the bodies of 252 people, said by Russia to be Ukrainian soldiers, were returned to Ukraine in an exchange, Ukraine’s Coordination Headquarters for the Treatment of Prisoners of War said Thursday. Russia received 25 bodies of Russian soldiers, Russian lawmaker Shamsail Saraliyev, a member of a parliamentary coordination group overseeing the exchanges, told RBC news outlet. ___ Follow the AP’s coverage of the war in Ukraine at https://apnews.com/hub/russia-ukraine This article originally appeared on Associated Press at https://www.yahoo.com/news/world/articles/russia-pounds-ukraines-capital-kyiv-071241165.html

articles.title: Senate debates in Michigan and Kansas put loyalty to Trump and America in focus
articles.summary: US Senate candidates Democrat Abdul El-Sayed, left, and Republican Mike Rogers shake hands after the debate on Wednesday, October 21, 2026, at WXYZ Channel 7 in Southfield, Michigan. - Robin Buckson/Pool/AP Michigan and Kansas held some of the final major Senate debates of the 2026 midterm elections on Wednesday night. And they were a study in contrasts. The Michigan Senate debate between Democratic nominee Abdul El-Sayed and Republican Mike Rogers was bitterly personal and ferociously contested — as befits a contest that could decide the chamber’s majority. Each candidate had a simple task. El-Sayed, the former executive director of the Detroit Health Department, needed to pin Rogers, a former congressman, to the deeply unpopular President Donald Trump and his economy — and to assuage questions from moderates about his politics. Rogers is trying to win in a state currently run by Democrats while dragging Trump’s historically low approval ratings behind him. His only hope is to disqualify El-Sayed as an acceptable senator in the eyes of voters. The debate in Kansas was a little more genial, with less focus on Trump and plenty of focus on whether Democratic pastor Adam Hamilton would be too allied with the political left — from which he repeatedly sought to distance himself — to unseat GOP Sen. Roger Marshall. And Marshall, much more than Rogers, made a point of overtly appealing to Trump’s voters. Here are takeaways from the two crucial debates: Fierce debate over El-Sayed’s loyalty Rogers raised an extraordinary question: Is El-Sayed, a Muslim who was born in Michigan, really loyal to the United States? The charge came against a backdrop of searing false claims by Trump that the Democrat is a “jihadist.” Rogers claimed El-Sayed — who would be the first Muslim elected to the Senate — was bought off by the Muslim Brotherhood , an Islamist group founded in Egypt, and that he had donors who supported Iran-backed extremist organizations like Hamas and Hezbollah. “If you are going to go to the United States Senate, we need to know: Are you for America or are you for these terrorist groups overseas?” Rogers asked. “You can grin and you can smile and you can talk real pretty, but I’m going to tell you what: That is a risk to our national security.” El-Sayed, who has repudiated the Brotherhood, accused his opponent of a “shameful” attack. “To bring into question my commitment to the Constitution is really beneath you. I am proud of America. I’m proud to be an American. I’m proud of our Constitution that guarantees all of us the right to pray as we choose to pray,” he said. unknown content item - ‘Pattern of deception’ vs. ‘MAGA bingo’ Rogers also sought to play into the conceit that El-Sayed, as a progressive, is too far to the left of Michigan’s electorate, and he tried to reopen splits that were exposed between rival factions during the Democratic primary. He claimed that El-Sayed was “aligned” with the Democratic Socialists of America and wants “bigger government and more taxes.” El-Sayed describes himself as a capitalist and is not a member of the DSA, but he is supported by several members of the group, including New York Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, who campaigned with him through Michigan’s Upper Peninsula last week. Rogers also tore at Democratic divides by appealing to disaffected supporters of El-Sayed’s defeated primary opponent. “You’re a Haley Stevens voter, and you came out of this, and you said, ‘Man, I just can’t do it. He’s too extreme’ … well, guess what, you have a home with us,” Rogers said in his closing statement. Ultimately, Rogers’ attacks on El-Sayed’s loyalties were aimed at advancing a broader argument — that the Democrat simply couldn’t be trusted — and one that implied, as Trump has, that he is not a fully authentic American. “There is, again, that whole pattern of deception,” Rogers said of El-Sayed’s claim to be in favor of strong border enforcement, using a refrain to which he frequently returned. Pushing back on El-Sayed’s denials that he wants to defund the police, Rogers claimed, “This guy has got new, false information about every 30 seconds.” El-Sayed countered multiple times that it was Rogers who was being untruthful and said he was playing a classic game of distraction practiced by Trump. He repeatedly said people should be playing “MAGA bingo” at home as they ticked off Rogers’ pre-planned buzzwords. But he warned: “When you are winning MAGA bingo, we are all losing.” The Trump factor Rogers, like every Republican candidate in the midterm elections, needs a way to separate himself from Trump’s most unpopular policies without alienating the president’s supporters, who must show up in vast numbers for him to win. He started with a complex pivot — admitting that the Michigan economy was in rough shape and that people were “hurting” but arguing that if Democrats got control of the Senate they’d make it even worse. This was a long way from Trump’s argument that Americans are living through an economic “golden age.” Rogers walked a fine line on tariffs, arguing that some were working to bring jobs home from Mexico and China, but that the trade war with Canada — a huge issue in Michigan’s border-state economy — was not well thought through. Rogers argued that Democratic control of Congress would cause higher taxes and higher costs, including for gasoline. El-Sayed had an easier task given huge public dissatisfaction with Trump’s handling of the economy; he claimed Rogers and the president stood “hip to hip.” He said that voters should send him to the Senate to ensure “money is going to be spent on you and your kids, rather than dropping bombs on somebody else and their kids.” He narrowed in on Rogers’ biggest vulnerability after the Republican said all his opponent did was say “Donald Trump” over and over again. El-Sayed countered by blaming the president’s decision to go to war with Iran for making the cost of living worse. “Yes, I am going to blame Donald Trump because this is Donald Trump’s economy. We are living in it,” El-Sayed said. “We are paying more for gas, more for groceries, defunding the Department of Education.” “We need to turn the page on Donald Trump, but that means we need to stand up to Donald Trump.” Kansas debate was more about Schumer than Trump Several states away, another Democratic Senate candidate was taking a very different approach. In red Kansas — a state Trump carried by 16 points — the name of the game for Hamilton was less about tying his opponent to Trump than assuring he’d be a candidate from the political middle. Republican Sen. Roger Marshall, right, and Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate Adam Hamilton participate in a debate at WDAF TV in Kansas City, Missouri, on October 21. - Charlie Riedel/Pool/AP In fact, Democratic Senate Leader Chuck Schumer earned more mentions than Trump, as Marshall repeatedly sought to pitch Hamilton as enabling and supporting the New York Democrat’s agenda. When asked how he differed from the Democratic Party, Hamilton said former President Joe Biden’s border policies were a “disaster” and that he’s “not somebody who favors the Socialist Party.” He said he didn’t support Medicare for All or the Green New Deal, though he liked “parts” of the latter. “We’ve heard Chuck Schumer mentioned, I don’t know, 50 times? … Maybe 20 times so far,” Hamilton said. “I find that interesting. I’ve already said I wouldn’t support Chuck Schumer for Senate majority leader if the Democrats [were] to control the Senate.” On the other side, Marshall distanced himself from Trump far less than Rogers has in Michigan. In fact, Marshall mostly bear-hugged Trump. When asked about Trump being unpopular even in Kansas, Marshall turned his response into an appeal to Trump supporters. “I’ve had multiple times when I’ve objected to the president before, but I do want to emphasize: We need the Trump voters to come out,” Marshall said. “And that would be my appeal tonight to people: If you want the Trump agenda to continue, if you want secure borders, if you want a strong military, if you want lower taxes … you need to come out, because we delivered on those things.” He also said later in the debate that Trump’s “tariffs are working.” When pressed again in his differences with Trump, he said he disagreed with ICE’s tactics in southwest Kansas — which many local Republicans recently objected to — and Trump’s plan to import beef. ICE was the big issue — and it got a little personal The ICE issue made for some of the most interesting portions of the debate, with Hamilton clearly seeking to turn it to his advantage. Marshall pitched the topic as an example of his ability to get Trump and his administration on the phone when he disagrees with something that’s happening. “The first thing I did when I saw what was going on in southwest Kansas (with ICE raids), I picked up the phone, called (Homeland Security) Secretary Markwayne Mullin and said, ‘Hey, I don’t think this is quite right. What’s going on?’” Marshall said. Marshall also signaled that there could be a broader conversation about immigration reform now that the border is more secure. He noted he has delivered many babies to undocumented parents. Hamilton pounced on that remark to cast the deportations that are currently taking place as heartless. “With all of those undocumented children that you delivered, did you also call ICE and ask them to be taken away?” Hamilton said. “What did you do with these people? You had compassion for them in delivering these children, but then you support quotas.” He said when he was in Hutchinson, Kansas, “There was a preschool teacher arrested in front of her children. That’s just not OK. We militarized and politicized ICE as opposed to them doing the important job they’re supposed to do, and that is protecting Americans from dangerous, dangerous people.” This story has been updated with additional details. articles.title: Meta strikes deal to keep Zuckerberg in California after wealth tax concerns
articles.summary: By Carlos Méndez Oct 21 (Reuters) - Meta Platforms has struck a deal with Mark Zuckerberg to keep him living in California after the CEO warned he was ‌considering leaving the state that houses the company's headquarters if voters pass a ‌wealth tax proposal next month. Under the deal, Zuckerberg will get non-voting shares he can sell to potentially foot ​a multi-billion-dollar tax bill in the event the proposal is approved, in exchange for a commitment to remain a resident of California, or wherever Meta maintains its headquarters, for eight years, Meta said on Wednesday. Zuckerberg, the world's sixth richest person according to Forbes, told Meta he was ‌considering moving his primary residence ⁠outside California because Proposition 40, a ballot measure dubbed the "California wealth tax", could expose him to a massive tax liability, potentially forcing him to ⁠sell voting shares to pay it. Proposition 40, which asks Californians whether to impose a one-time 5% tax on the state's billionaires, is far from certain to pass, political analysts say. The state ​is ​home to as many as 250 billionaires collectively ​worth upwards of $2 trillion. Zuckerberg, who has ‌a net worth of about $240 billion, can immediately sell 20% of the Class C shares he receives, representing 10% of his overall economic stake in the company, allowing him to pay a potential tax bill without losing voting control. The company said on Wednesday it will issue a new class of non-voting Class C common stock in January 2027, effectively resulting ‌in a two-for-one split, to fund acquisitions and ​retain top talent while maintaining Zuckerberg's control. Meta's long-term forecasts, ​as described in the filing, showed ​it would need to raise "hundreds of billions of dollars" over several ‌years, beginning as early as fall 2026, ​as it expects to ​need capital to finance its AI-related growth plan. The parent of Facebook and Instagram said a special committee of its board concluded it was "critically important" that Zuckerberg remain in ​a leadership role and continue ‌to manage the company from its California headquarters, particularly during what it described ​as "unprecedented challenge and competition in our industry" driven by AI. (Reporting by Carlos ​Méndez in Mexico City; Editing by Subhranshu Sahu) This article originally appeared on Reuters at https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/articles/meta-strikes-deal-keep-zuckerberg-020311745.html

articles.summary: 欧洲天然气市场正逼近新一轮供应危机，低库存与LNG供应受阻风险叠加，令冬季能源短缺担忧再度升温。 荷兰TTF前月期货本周早些时候升至2022年末以来最高水平，随后再度突破90欧元/兆瓦时。与去年冬季相比，天然气价格已接近三倍，欧洲工业、物流及居民用能成本面临进一步上涨压力。 供应端的压力主要来自欧洲库存不足与全球LNG贸易受扰。 欧盟储气设施填充率目前约为74%，降至彭博数据追溯至2009年以来的同期最低水平；与此同时，霍尔木兹海峡局势持续紧张，可能限制LNG供应，而欧洲还需与亚洲买家争夺有限的现货资源。 高盛大宗商品分析师Daan Struyven警告称， 如果霍尔木兹海峡LNG出口量仅维持正常水平的四分之一左右，同时严寒天气推高供暖需求，欧洲天然气价格可能进一步升至150欧元/兆瓦时。 随着冬季临近，寒潮与供应中断是否同时发生，将成为决定欧洲天然气市场压力的关键变量。 库存降至历史同期低位，天然气价格面临进一步上行压力 据Gas Infrastructure Europe数据，欧盟天然气库存今年以来首次出现下降，目前储气设施填充率约为74%，不仅明显低于同期15年历史均值，也是彭博数据追溯至2009年以来的同期最低水平。德国库存填充率更是仅有61%，缓冲空间尤为有限。 通常情况下，欧洲会在冬季取暖需求全面上升前积累充足库存，为寒潮和供应中断预留空间。 但今年较低的库存起点意味着，欧洲应对突发冲击的余地明显收窄。一旦气温骤降或LNG进口受阻，库存消耗可能加快，进一步推高现货采购需求与天然气价格。 与此同时，欧洲需要在国际市场上与亚洲买家争夺有限的LNG资源。霍尔木兹海峡局势若持续扰乱供应，全球可供交易的现货资源将进一步承压，欧洲买家可能不得不支付更高价格以争取货源。 天然气成本上升也将向工业生产、物流运输和居民供暖等领域传导，增加企业经营与家庭能源支出压力。 暖冬预期难消供应风险，寒潮与LNG中断是关键变量 天气变化将直接影响欧洲今冬的天然气供需平衡。目前，10月偏暖的气温抑制了供暖需求，为公用事业公司补充库存提供了一定空间。 最新预报显示，下周西北欧气温将再度回暖，但11月气温预计将明显下降，供暖需求能否持续保持低位仍存在不确定性。 部分市场观察人士认为，若今年冬季出现较强厄尔尼诺现象，欧洲可能迎来偏暖天气，从而缓解天然气消耗压力。但即使整体冬季气温偏高，阶段性寒潮仍可能导致需求短时间内大幅增加。若寒潮与LNG供应受阻同时发生，低库存将放大供需缺口，推动价格进一步飙升。 因此，欧洲天然气市场的关键风险不仅在于库存偏低，更在于供应与需求可能同时向不利方向变化。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 美联储先加息后或猛降息：AI 是利率关键阀门，开支拐点将触发政策转向！
articles.summary: 自沃什出任美联储主席以来，其多次在公开场合强调，AI驱动的生产率革命将压低长期通胀，使美联储能够在通胀不失控的前提下更早降息，从而复制1990年代格林斯潘时期由生产率繁荣支撑的低通胀、早降息局面。 然而，FOMC内部对于AI究竟将推升通胀还是抑制通胀，仍存在明显分歧。以沃什为代表的长期视角认为，AI将提升全要素生产率、降低边际成本并最终形成通缩效应，短期价格压力不应改变政策方向；但沃勒、古尔斯比、库克等官员更强调，当前AI基建投资主要体现为需求冲击。GPU、HBM等芯片及存储产品需求旺盛，叠加数据中心建设、电力供应和建筑劳动力等环节的产能约束，可能加剧核心商品价格与能源价格的上行压力；且AI相关投入品需求缺乏弹性，价格压力可能持续2-3年并向更广泛经济领域溢出。 此前9月FOMC会议纪要亦显示，与会者将“激增的AI相关投资”列为通胀压力来源，部分官员担心AI建设推动总需求超过总供给，另有官员则认为长期通胀预期仍锚定，而AI生产率红利尚待兑现。 这种分歧使美联储难以形成统一的反应函数：AI短期通胀效应具有现实数据支撑，而长期通缩效应需5-10年扩散期且时点不确定，美联储因而在“更快收紧以抑制AI需求过热”与“保持耐心以等待生产率红利”之间难以抉择。 更关键的是，上述分歧主要沿生产率渠道展开，而AI投资周期还通过资本开支渠道影响利率路径：短期内，AI投资扩张可能加剧对资本和融资资源的竞争，并通过抬升实际利率、通胀预期及期限溢价等渠道推高长期利率，使美债收益率面临高于市场预期的上行风险；中期一旦数据中心资本开支增速放缓、AI供应商融资链条转弱，AI投资便可能由增长动力转为拖累，迫使美联储降息应对。

articles.title: 谷歌Gemini 4 Carbon首批实测曝光，手感直逼Opus 5.5
articles.summary: Argon全面开放才8天，谷歌的下一张王牌，就杀进竞技场了！ 就在刚刚，谷歌最强的Carbon被曝开测。合作伙伴已经抢先拿到，LMArena上也开了盲测，发布就在眼前。 消息一出，测试者全扑进了Arena。 一天之内，Carbon的实测在X上炸成一片， 有人拿它一口气做完了整关超级玛丽。 上一代旗舰的热乎劲还没过，下一代就在门外排队了。 谷歌联创布林说， 谷歌开始踏上「RSI的跑步机」，模型正帮着造下一代模型。 超级玛丽一次通关，Carbon的3D强到离谱 Arena上的Carbon，名字还挂着「gemini-4-argon」。测试者认出它的办法说来好笑——就看慢不慢。 网友Harshith发现，挂这个名字的其实有两个模型。一个又快又不错，另一个慢得出奇，作品却真的惊艳，后者才是Carbon。 测评账号Lumina用超级玛丽的提示词，让Carbon做出了一整关游戏。 主角一路顶砖块、吃金币、钻水管，下到地下关再爬出来，最后跳上旗杆、走进城堡，屏幕弹出「COURSE CLEAR」，金币数和评级都结算了出来。 Lumina还把同一道体素宝塔题，交给Argon、Carbon、Opus 5.5和Sonnet 5.5同场比。 在Lumina看来，Carbon的质量明显要高过Argon，只是视任务不同，要慢2到4倍。 网友Synopsis的体素山谷，把画面又往上推了一层。 樱花沿着河岸开，红色拱桥架在水上，木屋亮着灯，一场雨说下就下，整片山谷跟着暗了下来。 网友Salio做了一座3D城堡，光照能在黄昏、蓝调时刻、月光和薄雾晨光之间切换，城下的石桥一路亮着灯。 知名爆料人chetaslua把Gemini的吉祥物交给Carbon，让它做一段讲碳为什么稳定的3D动画。 画面一开始，吉祥物盯着一颗碳-12原子核。随后6个电子按1s²2s²2p²排好，轨道杂化成4个一模一样的sp³瓣，再和邻居共享电子凑满8个，最后搭成一整块金刚石晶格。 chetaslua说，这道题对之前的Gemini模型来说非常难。拿Carbon讲碳，谷歌这次的命名，算是被网友玩明白了。 网友Salio做了一座3D城堡，光照能在黄昏、蓝调时刻、月光和薄雾晨光之间切换，城下的石桥一路亮着灯。 开发者Pankaj Kumar则让它做了一个能交互的3D水晶柑橘。 然而，到了SVG这一项，评价就开始分化了。 网友Binkg让Carbon画了一个可乐瓶的SVG，瓶身挂满水珠，标签上的小字和瓶盖都画了出来，旁边还能调霜冻、气泡和背光。 但Haleemah看了一整天的测试后说，Carbon最强的还是3D，好的SVG她还没见到。 SVG之外，前端也还是老问题。Lumina说，Carbon的前端设计和审美依旧平平，缺了Anthropic模型的那股味道。 同一个模型，3D能猛涨，前端却原地踏步，是因为两类题的考法不同。 3D场景里，几何、光照、碰撞全由代码决定，算错一点画面就崩， 对不对一眼就能验出来。 前端考的是留白多大、字号几号、按钮放哪，没有标准答案，只有人的偏好。 所以3D能靠算力和强化学习一路往上推，前端却只能靠大量人的反馈慢慢磨。 更慢但不偷懒，Carbon专治Argon的懒病 测试者晒作品时，几乎都会补一句慢，可很少有人抱怨，因为它不偷懒了。 偷懒，偏偏是Argon上线以来被骂得最狠的毛病。 它的跑分很漂亮，可开发者上手不到一周，「懒」的名声就传开了。 科技媒体Every测完Argon，给出了5条使用建议，第3条是让大家务必复核它的活。 在38次基准运行里，有17次，Argon把代码审查这一步打开又关上，中间只隔了30毫秒。 同一份建议里还藏着一组数字。把Argon从低推理档拉到高档，用时只变成原来的1.7倍；Opus 5.5拉到高档，要花18倍的时间。 也就是说，叫Argon多想一想，它也没多想多少。 到了Every CEO Dan Shipper的资深工程师基准上，Opus 5.5和Sonnet 5.5都拿了85%，GPT-6 Astra拿了81%，Argon只有21%，在8个模型里垫底。 而到了Carbon这里，情况直接反转。 Business Insider此前曝出，谷歌员工在内部试用Carbon后说，它写代码「感觉像极了Opus 5.5」。 Argon刚铺开就出Carbon，谷歌踏上RSI跑步机 从Argon到Carbon，谷歌这一轮的节奏快得惊人。 9月30日官宣Argon，先只交给Fairwind计划里的网络安全防御方；10月13日，Argon向开发者和订阅用户全面开放；又过了8天，Carbon就进了合作伙伴的测试。 谷歌出牌越来越快，布林给出的答案便是——RSI（递归自我改进）。 在最近一段圆桌对谈里，他曾表示，现在研究员已经和模型手拉手，一起做下一版模型了。 Argon的安全报告显示，今年9月，DeepMind超过九成的代码合并请求里，AI写的部分都在75%以上。 完全交给AI、人类插话不到3轮的合并请求，也从4月的7.5%涨到了11.9%。 DeepMind每月的代码合并请求，颜色越深，AI写的比例越高 当模型开始帮着造模型，Argon和Carbon挨得这么近，也就不难理解了。 本文来源： 新智元 风险提示及免责条款 articles.title: 四家中国车企，贡献欧盟车市前三季度近七成净增量
articles.summary: 作者 | 周智宇 欧盟车市今年前三季度同比多出的新车注册量中，近七成来自四家中国车企。 10月22日，欧洲汽车制造商协会（ACEA）公布最新数据，比亚迪、上汽、奇瑞和零跑前三季度在欧盟合计注册新车约60.24万辆，比去年同期增加31.21万辆。同期，欧盟全市场同比净增约46.05万辆。据此计算，四家企业贡献了67.8%的净增量，合计市场份额从3.60%升至7.07%。 比亚迪对上汽的反超，是其中最明显的变化。去年前三季度，比亚迪在欧盟还比上汽少卖约7.4万辆车，今年同期已领先约1.9万辆。比亚迪的市场份额从1.0%升至2.4%，上汽则从1.9%升至2.2%。两家都在扩大市场，距离却在一年间发生了逆转。 上汽并没有停下扩张。旗下MG在欧洲已经积累了较完整的销售网络，今年2月披露的经销伙伴超过1300家，覆盖34个欧洲国家。MG也在继续增加动力选择：在德国，最畅销车型ZS的混动版本占比超过八成，HS有三分之二客户选择插混；4月上市的纯电MG4 EV Urban，到9月底也已获得超过4000辆注册。 这组产品表现说明，上汽被反超很难简单归结为押错了动力路线。MG在德国前三季度的注册量仍增长近五成，上汽在欧盟的注册量也增长20.4%。问题在于，同一轮市场扩张中，比亚迪获得的新增注册量约为上汽的四倍，上汽的增长速度已经不足以守住两家之间的领先位置。 比亚迪的提速，接在一次欧洲业务调整之后。去年4月起，比亚迪持续补充欧洲经销商和熟悉当地市场的管理人员，并增加混动车型，修正早期进入欧洲时的不足。 变化在德国很直观。比亚迪2025年初在当地只有26个网点，到2026年6月已签下第200份经销商合同，合作伙伴陆续投入运营。到8月，其在德国的纯电和DM混动车型注册量已大致各占一半，SEAL U DM-i成为当月当地注册量最高的插混车型。 对比亚迪来说，国内已有的产品规模，需要经过当地车型选择和销售网络才能转化为销量。只提供纯电车，会漏掉仍希望保留加油便利的消费者；经销商覆盖不足，也会限制试驾、交付和维修。德国业务的变化显示，比亚迪正在同时扩大可服务的客群和销售覆盖。上汽较早积累的网络优势，面临着追赶者加快投入的压力。 奇瑞又进一步压缩了上汽的领先幅度。前三季度，其欧盟市场份额从0.5%升至1.6%，与上汽的注册量差距，从去年同期的约11.6万辆缩小至约5万辆。 奇瑞的增长更能说明，中国车企在欧洲获得的空间，并不局限于纯电市场。前三季度，纯电车在欧盟的份额升至22.7%，超过单列汽油车的21.2%，但非插电混动仍以36.3%的份额占据最大一块市场。混动和插混给了中国品牌接近传统燃油车用户的机会，这部分需求也同时被MG和比亚迪看中。 在西班牙，奇瑞旗下OMODA和JAECOO前三季度注册的新车中，近九成为非插电混动和插混，纯电约占5%。两品牌集中于紧凑型和中型SUV，切入的是家庭购车需求。这两个品牌在当地主要依靠混动SUV扩大规模，与MG的ZS、HS覆盖相近的产品市场。 几家企业的产品选择正在接近。MG的ZS、HS已有销售基础，比亚迪增加插混，奇瑞则扩大混动SUV销售。消费者可以在不同中国品牌间选择熟悉的车身形式和动力方案。对MG而言，早进入欧洲带来的优势仍在，但仅仅具备混动产品和本地网点，已经很难形成足够大的区隔。 混动业务的扩张还要放在新的贸易安排中考量。10月12日，商务部就中欧混动汽车磋商共识表示，双方已在2025年欧盟自中国进口30.2万辆混动汽车的基础上达成向上安排。比亚迪、上汽和奇瑞用混动扩大客群之后，后续供货还要结合相关规则。 零跑的追赶方式则有明显不同。其前三季度欧盟注册量约7.28万辆，市场份额从0.2%升至0.9%。在法国，零跑同期注册量中有93%为纯电，当地业务主要由纯电车型支撑。 零跑的不同之处在于，与Stellantis的合作同时解决了销售和服务体系的接入。进入法国约两年，零跑已经拥有150个销售网点，售后及备件物流可以利用Stellantis和Distrigo的现有网络。比亚迪在招募本地经销商、扩大覆盖，零跑则把车型接入了一个欧洲大型汽车集团的经营体系。 放到整个欧盟市场看，四家企业的份额仍在共同上升。同期，大众集团注册量增长0.7%，市场份额却从27.5%降至26.2%。欧洲车市总量恢复，伴随着增量向不同企业重新分配；中国品牌之间的排名变化，只是其中一部分。 混动SUV越来越多，本地网点也在铺开，几家中国车企正在争取相近的家庭买家。欧洲还容得下更多中国车，但后来者追得更快了。先到几年积累下的优势，已经不足以让一个品牌稳坐原来的位置。 articles.title: 死对头牵手！GPT住进Gemini家，OpenAI半年集齐三大云
articles.summary: 嚯，GPT要住进Gemini家了！ 就在今天，OpenAI和Google Cloud正式官宣了合作： GPT-6 Astra、GPT-6.1 Sol、GPT-6 Luna以及Codex，将正式上线Google Cloud。 首批模型目前已经开始向部分企业客户开放，接下来还会被塞进Google Antigravity和Gemini Agent。 不er，这俩不是还在大模型、搜索和编程Agent战场上狠狠干架吗？！ 怎么转眼间，死对头就秒变渠道合作方，还做起了彼此的生意？ 更关键的是，继Azure和AWS之后， OpenAI如今已正式集齐美国三大云厂商。 曾经牢牢锁在Azure里的OpenAI，正在彻底告别独家分销时代。 死对头，开始互相卖货了 目前， GPT-6 Astra 、 GPT-6.1 Sol 和 GPT-6 Luna 已进入Google Cloud的模型花园，并向部分企业客户开启私有预览。 企业可以直接通过Google Cloud的API调用这些模型，也可以把本地Codex CLI和桌面端工作流连进谷歌的Gemini平台，让Codex借道Google Cloud完成推理。 OpenAI称， 他们将会在未来几周内推出全面可用计划。 这次合作真正戳中企业客户心坎的可能有这两点： 1、企业可以直接在 Google Cloud Marketplace中 ，花谷歌云账户里钱买OpenAI家的模型。 2、 不同模型的调用费用可以合并到同一张Google Cloud账单里 ，甚至还能纳入跨模型的Flexible Savings Plans。 这意味着，以后企业们可以自由切换两家模型，不用重签合同，也不用另开账单。 想用的时候，直接在熟悉的Google Cloud工作环境里勾选就行了。 与此同时，企业还 能继续沿用Google Cloud已有的数据治理、安全和权限控制体系； 提示词、上下文和输出都留在指定的数据边界内，模型调用则要经过隔离网关和统一身份验证。 等未来OpenAI家的模型上线Google Antigravity和Gemini Agent后，大家便可以根据实际需求，灵活切换模型干活了。 Google Cloud对此也是颇为得意啊，忍不住在Blog中叉起腰来嘚瑟了一把： 我们已成为市场上唯一一家同时提供三大头部闭源大模型、外加200多款自研、第三方及开源模型的超大规模云厂商！ OpenAI半年集齐三大云 看到这里，肯定有小伙伴要问了： 等等，OpenAI此前不是被Azure独家绑定了吗？ 没错。 过去，Azure一直握着OpenAI无状态API的独家云分销权。 哪怕OpenAI与其他厂商合作，相关API调用原则上仍要跑在Azure上。 但就在今年 4月27日 ，这层独家绑定终于松动了。 微软和OpenAI重新修改了合作协议，并划掉了这条独家限制。 从此以后，OpenAI可以通过任何一家云平台向客户提供产品，而微软所持有的OpenAI模型与产品授权也改为非独家。 门锁刚打开，OpenAI第二天就闪身进了AWS。 4月28日 ，GPT和Codex火速搬进了Amazon Bedrock。 AWS客户可以直接用原有身份和企业控制体系调用模型，相关费用也能抵扣既有云消费承诺。 如今，OpenAI又一脚迈进了Google Cloud。 而从Azure独家，到AWS，再到Google Cloud，OpenAI 只用了半年时间 ，便把模型铺进了美国三大云厂商。 企业业务扎在哪片云里，它就追到哪片云里摆摊，主打一个 走到哪儿、卖到哪儿 。 同时，微软也没有被OpenAI甩下车。 照4月的新协议， 微软目前仍是OpenAI的主要云合作伙伴，OpenAI产品也会优先登陆Azure。 不愧是初恋啊，地位稳稳的。 只不过，Azure不再独家，隔壁的AWS和Google Cloud也终于能卖上同款了。 模型狠狠干架，云厂商闷声收钱 大家也都知道啊，GPT和Gemini可是老对家了，天天在擂台上干架。 那OpenAI和Google Cloud为什么又突然牵起了手？ 其实 这俩都把自己的小算盘打得噼啪响。 OpenAI图的是企业客户。 因为企业采购AI模型，看的早已不止是谁在榜单上高了几分。 数据存在哪里、现有合同签给谁、安全和审计体系跑在哪朵云上，同样会直接左右最终选择。 所以，OpenAI开始顺着云厂商已经铺好的客户关系往里钻。 企业把业务放在Azure，它就在Azure卖；业务跑在AWS，它就钻进Bedrock； 数据扎在Google Cloud，它又把GPT和Codex端到模型花园里。 客户不用专门绕进OpenAI自己的API平台，GPT就能自己进入客户每天工作的地方。 Google Cloud图的则是平台生意。 客户选择Gemini，谷歌可以直接赚模型的钱； 客户选择GPT，模型虽是对手家的，谷歌依然守住了Marketplace、云基础设施、数据治理和安全服务。 甚至模型打得越凶，企业越想根据不同任务来回切换，Google Cloud这座模型商场的价值就越高。 至于企业嘛，其实图的就是两个字： 省事。 不用搬数据，不用换云平台，不用另签一套供应商合同，便能按照能力、延迟和成本，把不同任务分别塞给Gemini、GPT或Claude。 以前大家选模型多少带点“押中一家、全家跟上”的味道； 但现在，同一套云平台里已经摆出一整排货架，谁好用就点谁，谁便宜就切谁，真真是方便多了。 路透社也将其概括为一个更广泛的行业趋势： 微软、AWS和Google Cloud这样的超大规模云厂商，正在成为前沿模型实验室最重要的商业分销渠道。 其中，模型公司负责造货、卷能力； 云厂商则负责握住企业客户、采购入口和结算体系，再从每笔交易里抽走一份。 所以，模型擂台上，GPT和Gemini以后该打还是得打； 但走下擂台，Google Cloud已经默默给GPT摆好了货架。 竞争归竞争，生意归生意，硅谷这群人果然一个比一个会过日子（doge）。 One More Thing 搞笑的是，该牵的手牵了，但该掐的架，奥特曼和劈柴这俩活宝也一点没少掐。 前不久，奥特曼还在阴阳： Google只是在给搜索等老产品外挂AI，OpenAI从头搭起的AI原生产品才是王道。 转眼间，劈柴就在同一档Alex Kantrowitz播客里狠狠呛了回去： Gemini App本来就是从头开始做的AI产品。 照这个逻辑， 大家如今都在往产品里塞Agent，OpenAI是不是也在给ChatGPT外挂Agent？ 回旋镖刚飞完一圈，第二天，GPT就被端上了Google Cloud。 嗯……你俩就继续这么相爱相杀下去吧。 本文来源： 量子位 风险提示及免责条款 articles.title: 未来美元中心或边际削弱，中国现房新政推动销售模式转型，新旧动能转换关键在于技术扩散---1022宏观脱水
articles.summary: 2010至2026年美国经济从低增长低通胀低利率高债务的脆弱修复，转向财政主导、高赤字支撑、再通胀反复与结构分化加剧。美国财政问题本质是高赤字、高利息、高融资成本的自我强化。美债从无条件避险资产转向有条件避险资产，全球避险体系向三层锚复合结构重构。 8月28日住房销售制度新政落地后，7城出台配套细则，改革目标为降低期房交付风险，推动销售模式由高杠杆预售向现房、晚预售转型。政策抬高预售门槛并强化资金监管，设置过渡期缓释供给冲击，对二三线城市土地成交影响较大，新房供给短期存在缺口、中长期结构调整。 美国信息技术革命通过资本深化与效率提升推动生产率加速，日本制造业优势未能充分带动非制造业效率改善，韩国面临大小企业生产率差距。新兴产业快速发展并不必然带来整体经济增长提速，关键在于新技术能否带动整体经济提效，存量调整方式也影响新动能成长。

articles.title: 宇树10周年，王兴兴：我劝你相信AI
articles.summary: 10 月 22 日，杭州国际博览中心热闹非常，不仅人多，而且机器人也特别多。 这是 2026 年宇树科技举办的世界物理 AI 大会的现场，从四足机器人到人形机器人，你甚至可以说这里是全球「机器人密度」最高的地方。 2026 年，也是宇树科技创立的第十年。有意思的是，在今天的舞台上，宇树科技创始人王兴兴，在谈机器人之外，聊的最多的就是当下最火热的 AI。 他不仅劝所有人要「相信 AI」，而且还反思，觉得自己「相信 AI 还相信得不够」 。 为什么这家中国、乃至全球机器人行业中最有实力的公司掌舵者，会这么说？物理 AI 的拐点，真的要到来了吗？ 必须相信 AI 在王兴兴 36 分钟的演讲中，宇树自己的产品只占了开头和结尾。中间最长的一段，王兴兴在做一件事——劝人相信 AI。 从 AI 攻下了一批顶尖数学难题，「人类最智慧的金字塔的尖端」已经被击穿；到 AI 逆向工程让「传统软件公司的壁垒没了」；AI 视频里人物的表情和情绪「比真人演的还好很多」；顶尖大模型公司内部「已经实现了模型的自进化」。 「这不是闹着玩的」。他的结论是，以当下的模型能力，哪怕不再进步，信息世界也已经被「完全击穿」。 然后他说了一句不太像上市公司董事长会说的话，「 我感觉我自己还不够相信，还不够坚定 」。 这不是即兴发挥。十天前的上海工博会上，他已经当众「认错」过一次，「过去十几年我犯的最大的错误，就是对 AI 的相信还不太够」。他还给过一个倍数，5 年前或 10 年前你喜欢、相信 AI 的程度，「现在乘 10 倍都不为过」。 王兴兴在会上探讨物理 AI 的未来｜图片来源：宇树科技 更直观的变化在时间表上。今年 8 月的世界机器人大会，王兴兴对具身智能「ChatGPT 时刻」的预期还是快则 2 到 3 年、慢则 5 到 10 年；两个月后，这个窗口被他压缩成「1 到 2 年，慢的话 2 到 3 年」。至于随便把一台宇树机器人带进陌生的家里，一句话让它把房间收拾好，「快的话可能明年就可以实现」。工博会上他说得更直白，「明年 GPT-7 出来，可能直接把具身智能问题打穿」。 一个硬件出身的工程师，在两个月里成了全场最激进的 AI 布道者。这看上去像一次认知突变，但把宇树最近半年的处境摊开来看， 他的「相信」几乎是一道必答题。 但是，宇树的强项——机器人本体，依然是王兴兴骄傲的事情。 王兴兴在台上最骄傲的是 G1。这款 2024 年 5 月发布的人形机器人， 累计下线大约 1 到 2 万台 ，他称之为全球单一型号出货量最大的人形机器人。 10 月 21 日，宇树放出 H2-X「功夫传奇 守护」的视频，一脚踢瘪车门、徒手抬车、4 米高台空翻落地，续航从 H2 的约 3 小时拉到约 8 小时。可以看到，宇树团队依然在快速迭代公司的产品。 本体之外，一直在布道 AI 的王兴兴，推销的 AI，并不完全是宇树自己的 AI。 随后的论坛环节王兴兴和姚明等嘉宾一同探讨物理 AI 的未来｜图片来源：宇树科技 他在台上很坦白，「我们毕竟是一家新公司」，跟全球最头部的多模态大模型公司「做一模一样的模型，那是不太现实的」。宇树会自研，也会和国内外大模型公司合作。他展示的最亮眼的 demo，是把 GPT-6 接到机器人上，零训练就能自己洗笔、换颜料，在围棋盘上精准落子。他判断规划和导航这类问题「某种意义上已经解决掉了」，剩下的是多模态大模型的输入输出和真实机器人之间的对齐——传感器的误差、执行器的误差，「我觉得这个也是很快可以解决的问题」。 把这几句话连起来，就能看清这份「信仰」背后的商业逻辑。 如果机器人的大脑最终由 OpenAI、谷歌这样的公司提供，而且像他说的那样越来越强、越来越便宜，那具身智能这场竞赛的胜负手，就会回到谁能最便宜、最大规模地造出可靠的身体。 这恰恰是宇树最擅长的事。 所以在王兴兴列出的未来最重要的几件事里，排第一的不是模型，而是硬件的大规模制造能力。宇树现在一年生产几万台机器人、几十万个关节电机，在他看来「完全不够」，真正普及至少要「年产千万台」。他甚至谈到了算力集群、芯片产能和矿。至于宇树自己的模型能力，他押注的是一套「自进化」循环，让 AI 自己检索论文、写控制代码、在仿真里训练、到真机上测试，再把打分结果喂回去。这套方法的前提同样是基础模型每个月都在变强，用他的话说，「模型能力越提升」，这个循环「也会越来越强」。 世界物理 AI 大赛启动｜图片来源：宇树科技 换句话说， 对一家机器人公司而言，「相信 AI」不是锦上添花的表态，而是整套战略成立的前提。 AI 进步得越快，宇树的硬件规模优势就越早兑现。 演讲的最后，王兴兴讲了一条自己和 AI 的「交叉时间线」。2009 年上大一，他做的第一台机器人就是双足人形；大学一门计算机课要写小论文，他的题目是「随着神经网络规模的增加，能力会越来越强」，理由是人的大脑比鸡、狗、猪的大，所以人更聪明。然后是 2016 年的 AlphaGo，以及 2022 年底的 ChatGPT，后者直接促成了宇树 2023 年正式进军人形机器人。 这段回忆讲得很真诚，也很有选择性，它把一个硬件工程师的十几年，讲成了一条始终指向 AI 的直线。也许他确实很早就相信了，只是相信得不够；也许是这个时代逼着每一家机器人公司，都必须讲出同一个故事。 展台的热闹之外 在这届宇树举办的世界物理 AI 大会上，展台区域可以说是机器人比人多的经典场景。除了传统的擂台赛、打乒乓球等 showcase 之外，你甚至还能看到抖空竹、玩「剑玉」的机器人——是的，玩剑玉这个机器人的开发者说的是日语。 玩「剑玉」的机器人｜图片来源：极客公园 各种各样形态的机器狗｜图片来源：极客公园 在整个展区我们能看到，目前无论是四足还是人形机器人，最大的一个场景，可能还是导览和娱乐。例如你可以看到戴着牛仔帽的 G1 机器人，也能看到被打扮成熊猫、恐龙和舞狮的四足机器狗。一家叫逸璟科技的公司，还为机器人配上了能做出表情的「人脸」，团队负责人告诉极客公园，在一些康养、导览等场景，有一张「人脸」的机器人，还是会比普通的机器人，更让人感到亲近，虽然有一些些「恐怖谷」效应。 此外，安全、巡逻等场景，也在真正意义上的落地。一家改造机器狗做巡逻场景的负责人告诉极客公园，配上激光雷达和相关设备的四足机器狗，已经能代替人工在夜晚进行小区、园区的执勤工作，遇到危急情况，人类操作员还能进行远程操作。而如果背上一些灭火设备，这些四足机器人还能完成灭火等任务。 工作人员正在遥操操作｜图片来源：极客公园 展区中比较热的一个展台，是机器人教育和课程的展台。宇树的同学告诉极客公园，团队有成熟的方案，不仅能提供硬件，而且能提供从硬件、软件和人才的一套方案，为学校提供整套的机器人教育实验室，让更多的学生，能真正上手体验机器人编程的魅力。 学习投篮的机器人｜图片来源：极客公园 在大会当场，王兴兴和一众嘉宾，也开启了世界物理 AI 大赛，宇树提供高达数千万人民币的奖金，鼓励全球开发者进行机器人的开发，这也是自大疆曾经的「RoboMaster」大赛之后，国内少见的真正培养机器人开发者的大赛。 正如这几年新一波的 AI 浪潮，培养出了无数的 AI 创业者和超级个体一样，当物理 AI 开始进入临界状态时，这个行业同样需要无数的机器人人才，而世界物理 AI 大赛，无疑是个很好的起点。 本文来源： 极客公园 风险提示及免责条款
